105	def _prepare_missing_values(columns):
106	    """Validate the optional ``missing_values`` marker list of each column.
107	
108	    Returns a mapping of output field name to a fresh list of the declared
109	    markers, each trimmed of surrounding whitespace. The attribute must be
110	    a non-empty list of strings; an entry that trims to empty or repeats
111	    an earlier trimmed entry (compared case-sensitively) is invalid.
112	    Raises ValueError naming ``missing_values``, the output field and the
113	    offending value before the input is read; the caller's schema is
114	    never mutated.
115	    """
116	    missing = {}
117	    for column in columns:
118	        name = column["name"]
119	        if "missing_values" not in column:
120	            continue
121	        values = column["missing_values"]
122	        if not isinstance(values, list) or not values:
123	            raise ValueError(
124	                f"column {name!r} missing_values {values!r} must be a non-empty list")
125	        checked = []
126	        for entry in values:
127	            if not isinstance(entry, str):
128	                raise ValueError(
129	                    f"column {name!r} missing_values entry {entry!r} must be a string")
130	            marker = entry.strip()
131	            if not marker:
132	                raise ValueError(
133	                    f"column {name!r} missing_values entry {entry!r} must not be blank")
134	            if marker in checked:
135	                raise ValueError(
136	                    f"column {name!r} missing_values entry {entry!r} is repeated")
137	            checked.append(marker)
138	        missing[name] = checked
139	    return missing

142	def _validate_schema_structure(schema):
143	    """Validate the structural shape of the schema before any file is read.
144	
145	    The schema must be an object holding a non-empty ``columns`` list;
146	    each column must be an object carrying ``name`` (a non-blank string,
147	    kept verbatim -- never trimmed -- and unique case-sensitively) and
148	    ``type`` (one of ``string``, ``integer``, ``boolean``), plus an
149	    optional ``required`` that, when present, must be a boolean. Checks
150	    run top level first, then column by column in order (column
151	    structure, name, duplicate name, type, required) and only the first
152	    problem is reported: the ValueError message names ``schema`` and the
153	    one-based column position, names a missing key, carries the
154	    offending value verbatim, and points a duplicate name at the later
155	    column. Unknown attributes are ignored and the caller's schema is
156	    never mutated.
157	    """
158	    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
159	        raise ValueError(f"schema must be an object, got {schema!r}")
160	    if "columns" not in schema:
161	        raise ValueError("schema is missing 'columns'")
162	    columns = schema["columns"]
163	    if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
164	        raise ValueError(f"schema 'columns' must be a non-empty list, got {columns!r}")
165	    seen = {}
166	    for index, column in enumerate(columns, start=1):
167	        if not isinstance(column, dict):
168	            raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} must be an object, got {column!r}")
169	        for key in ("name", "type"):
170	            if key not in column:
171	                raise ValueError(f"schema column {index} is missing {key!r}")
172	        name = column["name"]
173	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
174	            raise ValueError(
175	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} must be a non-blank string")
176	        if name in seen:
177	            raise ValueError(
178	                f"schema column {index} name {name!r} duplicates column {seen[name]}")
179	        seen[name] = index
180	        kind = column["type"]
181	        if kind not in ("string", "integer", "boolean"):
182	            raise ValueError(
183	                f"schema column {index} type {kind!r} must be one of "
184	                "'string', 'integer', 'boolean'")
185	        if "required" in column and not isinstance(column["required"], bool):
186	            raise ValueError(
187	                f"schema column {index} required {column['required']!r} must be a boolean")
188

190	def _prepare_schema(schema):
191	    _validate_schema_structure(schema)
192	    columns = schema["columns"]
193	    defaults = _prepare_defaults(columns)
194	    allowed = _prepare_allowed_values(columns, defaults)
195	    markers = _prepare_missing_values(columns)
196	    sources = []
197	    for column in columns:
198	        name = column["name"]
199	        if "source" not in column:
200	            sources.append(name)
201	            continue
202	        origin = column["source"]
203	        if not isinstance(origin, str) or not origin.strip():
204	            raise ValueError(f"column {name!r}: source must be a non-empty, non-blank string")
205	        sources.append(origin)
206	    owners = {}
207	    for column, origin in zip(columns, sources):
208	        name = column["name"]
209	        if origin in owners:
210	            raise ValueError(f"columns {owners[origin]!r} and {name!r} share source {origin!r}")
211	        owners[origin] = name
212	    return columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers

215	def _prepare_duplicate_by(duplicate_by, names):
216	    """Validate the optional duplicate-report fields against output names.
217	
218	    Returns a new list or None when reporting is disabled. Raises ValueError
219	    before the input is opened.
220	    """
221	    if duplicate_by is None:
222	        return None
223	    if not isinstance(duplicate_by, list):
224	        raise ValueError("duplicate_by must be a list of schema field names")
225	    if not duplicate_by:
226	        raise ValueError("duplicate_by must not be empty")
227	    known = set(names)
228	    seen = set()
229	    for member in duplicate_by:
230	        if not isinstance(member, str) or not member.strip():
231	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate_by entry {member!r} must be a non-blank string")
232	        if member in seen:
233	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate_by field {member!r} is repeated")
234	        if member not in known:
235	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate_by field {member!r} is not a schema column name")
236	        seen.add(member)
237	    return list(duplicate_by)

240	def _find_duplicates(records, duplicate_by):
241	    """Group accepted records by the converted values of duplicate_by fields."""
242	    groups = {}
243	    for record_number, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
244	        value_key = tuple(record[field] for field in duplicate_by)
245	        groups.setdefault(value_key, []).append(record_number)
246	    return [
247	        {"key": dict(zip(duplicate_by, values)), "record_numbers": numbers}
248	        for values, numbers in groups.items()
249	        if len(numbers) > 1
250	    ]

253	def _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns):
254	    """Validate the optional single-field equality filter.
255	
256	    The condition is an object with exactly ``field`` and ``value`` keys;
257	    field matches an output name literally (source aliases are not
258	    recognized) and value must fit the target type, with null allowed for
259	    every type. Returns (field, value) or None when filtering is disabled.
260	    Raises ValueError before the input is read.
261	    """
262	    if filter_eq is None:
263	        return None
264	    if not isinstance(filter_eq, dict):
265	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must be an object with 'field' and 'value' keys")
266	    keys = set(filter_eq)
267	    if keys != {"field", "value"}:
268	        details = []
269	        missing = [key for key in ("field", "value") if key not in keys]
270	        extra = sorted(keys - {"field", "value"})
271	        if missing:
272	            details.append("missing key(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
273	        if extra:
274	            details.append("unexpected key(s): " + ", ".join(extra))
275	        raise ValueError("filter_eq must contain exactly 'field' and 'value' keys (" + "; ".join(details) + ")")
276	    field = filter_eq["field"]
277	    if not isinstance(field, str):
278	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a string")
279	    if not field.strip():
280	        raise ValueError("filter_eq field must be a non-blank string")
281	    by_name = {column["name"]: column for column in columns}
282	    if field not in by_name:
283	        raise ValueError(f"filter_eq field {field!r} is not a schema column name")
284	    value = filter_eq["value"]
285	    kind = by_name[field]["type"]
286	    if value is not None:
287	        if kind == "string" and not isinstance(value, str):
288	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a string or null")
289	        if kind == "integer" and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int)):
290	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a non-boolean integer or null")
291	        if kind == "boolean" and not isinstance(value, bool):
292	            raise ValueError(f"filter_eq value for field {field!r} must be a boolean or null")
293	    return field, value

296	def _build_result(records, errors, duplicate_fields, filter_condition):
297	    """Apply the equality filter to fully validated records, then counts."""
298	    if filter_condition is None:
299	        kept, filtered_count = records, 0
300	    else:
301	        field, expected = filter_condition
302	        kept = [record for record in records if record[field] == expected]
303	        filtered_count = len(records) - len(kept)
304	    result = {"records": kept, "errors": errors, "accepted": len(kept),
305	              "rejected": len(errors)}
306	    if filter_condition is not None:
307	        result["filtered"] = filtered_count
308	    if duplicate_fields is not None:
309	        result["duplicates"] = _find_duplicates(kept, duplicate_fields)
310	    return result

317	    offending record's starting physical line (header is line 1; a data
318	    record starts on the physical line after the preceding row ends), and

326	def _csv_error_reason(exc):
327	    """Map a strict-reader ``csv.Error`` onto the two fatal quote problems.
328	
329	    ``strict=True`` raises "unexpected end of data" for a quoted field
330	    still open at EOF and "',' expected after '\"'" for any character
331	    other than comma/newline/EOF right after a closing quote (spaces and
332	    tabs included). Anything else is reported verbatim.
333	    """
334	    message = str(exc)
335	    if message == "unexpected end of data":
336	        return ("unterminated quoted field: a double-quoted field was still "
337	                "open when the file ended")
338	    if "expected after" in message:
339	        return ("invalid text after closing quote: only a comma, a line "
340	                "ending or the end of the file may follow a closing "
341	                "double quote")
342	    return message

345	def normalize_csv(source, schema, duplicate_by=None, filter_eq=None):
346	    columns, sources, defaults, allowed, markers = _prepare_schema(schema)
347	    names = [column["name"] for column in columns]
348	    duplicate_fields = _prepare_duplicate_by(duplicate_by, names)
349	    filter_condition = _prepare_filter_eq(filter_eq, columns)
350	    records, errors = [], []
351	    # strict=True turns the two quote-syntax problems that a lenient reader
352	    # silently folds into the data into csv.Error: a quoted field still open
353	    # at EOF and any character other than comma/newline/EOF right after a
354	    # closing quote (a space or tab included). A doubled "" inside a quoted
355	    # field still decodes to one literal double quote, and a double quote
356	    # inside an unquoted field stays an ordinary character.
357	    with Path(source).open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
358	        reader = csv.reader(handle, strict=True)
359	        # reader.line_num is the physical line where the row just read ends;
360	        # LF, CRLF (counted once) and a lone CR all terminate a line. A
361	        # record's starting physical line is one past the end of the
362	        # preceding row, so skipped empty lines and newlines inside quoted
363	        # fields shift it down. When the strict reader reports a syntax
364	        # error the failing record starts on previous_end + 1, even though
365	        # the problem is only detected at a later physical line or at EOF.
366	        previous_end = 0
367	        header = None
368	        try:
369	            for cells in reader:
370	                start_line = previous_end + 1
371	                previous_end = reader.line_num
372	                if header is None:
373	                    header = cells
374	                    if header != sources:
375	                        raise ValueError(
376	                            "CSV header must match schema column sources and order exactly")
377	                    continue
378	                if not cells:
379	                    # An ordinary empty physical line: skipped as a record but it
380	                    # still occupies a physical line number (tracked above).
381	                    continue
382	                record = {}
383	                row_errors = []
384	                if len(cells) != len(sources):
385	                    row_errors.append("wrong number of cells")
386	                else:
387	                    for column, value in zip(columns, cells):
388	                        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
389	                        value = value.strip()

519	            if row_errors:

544	def _stage_jsonl(destination, records):
545	    """Serialize records into a temp file in the destination's directory.
546	
547	    Parent directories are never created and the destination is not
548	    touched. Returns (staged_path, existed); raised OSError names the
549	    target path.
550	    """
551	    target = Path(destination)
552	    parent = target.parent
553	    if not parent.exists() or not parent.is_dir():
554	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: parent directory does not exist")
555	    if target.exists() and target.is_dir():
556	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: target is a directory")
557	    if target.exists() and not os.access(target, os.W_OK):
558	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: target is not writable")
559	    payload = "".join(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for record in records)
560	    try:
561	        handle, staged_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
562	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent)
563	    except OSError as exc:
564	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
565	    staged = parent / staged_name
566	    try:
567	        out = os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="")
568	    except BaseException:
569	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
570	            os.close(handle)
571	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
572	            staged.unlink()
573	        raise
574	    try:
575	        with out:
576	            out.write(payload)
577	    except OSError as exc:
578	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
579	            staged.unlink()
580	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
581	    except BaseException:
582	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
583	            staged.unlink()
584	        raise
585	    return staged, target.exists() and not target.is_dir()

588	def _install_staged(target, staged, existed):
589	    """Replace target with staged, keeping its old bytes recoverable.
590	
591	    Returns the backup path (or None). If the swap fails after the
592	    original was moved aside, the original is restored at target before
593	    the OSError (naming target) is raised.
594	    """
595	    mode = None
596	    backup = None
597	    try:
598	        if existed:
599	            mode = target.stat().st_mode & 0o7777
600	            # Reserve a unique backup name so an unrelated user file can
601	            # never be clobbered; os.replace below overwrites the empty
602	            # placeholder with the original file.
603	            backup_handle, backup_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
604	                prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".backup", dir=target.parent)
605	            os.close(backup_handle)
606	            backup = target.parent / backup_name
607	            os.replace(target, backup)
608	        os.replace(staged, target)
609	        if mode is not None:
610	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
611	                target.chmod(mode)
612	        else:
613	            # mkstemp creates 0600; a freshly created output historically
614	            # got the usual 0666 & ~umask mode from open().
615	            umask = os.umask(0)
616	            os.umask(umask)
617	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
618	                target.chmod(0o666 & ~umask)
619	    except OSError as exc:
620	        if backup is not None:
621	            if target.exists():
622	                # The original never left target; just drop the placeholder.
623	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
624	                    backup.unlink()
625	            else:
626	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
627	                    os.replace(backup, target)
628	        raise OSError(f"cannot write {target}: {exc}") from None
629	    return backup

632	def _write_jsonl_outputs_atomic(output_path, records, errors_path, errors):
633	    """Write both JSONL outputs as one all-or-nothing operation.
634	
635	    Either both files are fully written (replacing existing files), or a
636	    filesystem failure leaves every target exactly as it was beforehand:
637	    pre-existing files keep their bytes and previously absent files stay
638	    absent. Parent directories are never created.
639	    """
640	    output_target, errors_target = Path(output_path), Path(errors_path)
641	    staged_output, output_existed = _stage_jsonl(output_target, records)
642	    try:
643	        staged_errors, errors_existed = _stage_jsonl(errors_target, errors)
644	    except BaseException:
645	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
646	            staged_output.unlink()
647	        raise
648	    installs = []
649	    try:
650	        installs.append((output_target,
651	                         _install_staged(output_target, staged_output, output_existed)))
652	        installs.append((errors_target,
653	                         _install_staged(errors_target, staged_errors, errors_existed)))
654	    except BaseException:
655	        # Undo only fully completed installs; a failed _install_staged
656	        # has already restored that target itself.
657	        for target, backup in installs:
658	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
659	                if backup is not None:
660	                    os.replace(backup, target)
661	                else:
662	                    target.unlink()
663	        for leftover in (staged_errors, staged_output):
664	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
665	                leftover.unlink()
666	        raise
667	    for _, backup in installs:
668	        if backup is not None:
669	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
670	                backup.unlink()

673	def _check_path_isolation(source, schema, output, errors):
674	    """Reject when an output aliases an input or the other output.
675	
676	    Runs before either input is read or either output is written. Two
677	    paths alias when their resolved pathnames are equal (identical paths,
678	    including relative/absolute spellings and symbolic-link aliases) or,
679	    when both paths currently exist, when they share a device and inode
680	    (distinct hard links to the same file). Outputs that do not exist yet
681	    only take part in the pathname comparison, so two fresh names are not
682	    refused merely because they could later be linked together. File
683	    names, extensions and directories never decide identity, and two
684	    independent files with identical contents are always allowed. Any I/O
685	    error resolving or stating a path propagates as OSError naming it.
686	    """
687	    roles = (
688	        ("source", Path(source)),
689	        ("schema", Path(schema)),
690	        ("records output", Path(output)),
691	        ("errors output", Path(errors)),
692	    )
693	
694	    def resolve(path):
695	        try:
696	            return path.resolve()
697	        except OSError as exc:
698	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {path}: {exc}") from None
699	
700	    def file_identity(labeled_path, resolved):
701	        try:
702	            result = resolved.stat()
703	        except FileNotFoundError:
704	            return None
705	        except OSError as exc:
706	            raise OSError(f"cannot check path {labeled_path}: {exc}") from None
707	        return result.st_dev, result.st_ino
708	
709	    entries = [(label, path, resolve(path)) for label, path in roles]
710	    # Pairs involving at least one output, in a fixed order: the two
711	    # outputs, then records output against the inputs, then errors output.
712	    pairs = ((2, 3), (2, 0), (2, 1), (3, 0), (3, 1))
713	    for left_index, right_index in pairs:
714	        left_label, left_path, left_resolved = entries[left_index]
715	        right_label, right_path, right_resolved = entries[right_index]
716	        if left_resolved == right_resolved:
717	            raise ValueError(
718	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
719	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same file")
720	        left_identity = file_identity(left_path, left_resolved)
721	        right_identity = file_identity(right_path, right_resolved)
722	        # A not-yet-existing path (or a dangling link to one) cannot
723	        # currently be hard-linked to an existing file; the resolved
724	        # pathname comparison above still applies to both spellings.
725	        if left_identity is None or right_identity is None:
726	            continue
727	        if left_identity == right_identity:
728	            raise ValueError(
729	                f"paths must be distinct: {left_label} {left_path} and "
730	                f"{right_label} {right_path} point to the same existing file")

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from data_importer import normalize_csv, normalize_jsonl, write_jsonl

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def run_cli(source, output, errors, fmt=None, extra=()):
    command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(source),
               "--schema", str(ROOT / "samples/schema.json"),
               "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors)]
    if fmt is not None:
        command += ["--format", fmt]
    command += list(extra)
    return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)


def hidden_entries(directory):
    return [path.name for path in Path(directory).iterdir() if path.name.startswith(".")]



class ImporterTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.schema = json.loads((ROOT / "samples/schema.json").read_text())

    def test_types_whitespace_and_optional_null(self):
        result = normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["accepted"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["records"][0], {"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": True})
        self.assertIsNone(result["records"][1]["orders"])

    def test_row_errors_preserve_valid_rows(self):
        result = normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/mixed.csv", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 2))
        self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [3, 4])
        self.assertIn("orders", result["errors"][0]["errors"][0])

    def test_invalid_schema_and_header(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", {"columns": [{"name": "name", "type": "date"}]})
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            normalize_csv(ROOT / "samples/customers.csv", {"columns": [{"name": "other", "type": "string"}]})

    def mapped_schema(self):
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True, "source": "display_name"},
            {"name": "orders", "type": "integer", "source": "purchase_count"},
            {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "required": True},
        ]}

    def write_csv(self, directory, text):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def write_csv_bytes(self, directory, data):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return path

    def test_physical_rows_blank_and_multiline_fixture(self):
        text = ("name,orders,active\n\n\"Ma\nya\",3,true\nBad,x,true\n"
                "\"No\nra\",2,\nZ,3,false\n")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema, duplicate_by=["orders"])
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 2))
        self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [5, 6])
        self.assertIn("orders", result["errors"][0]["errors"][0])
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][1]["errors"], ["active: required value is empty"])
        self.assertEqual([record["name"] for record in result["records"]], ["Ma\nya", "Z"])
        self.assertEqual(result["duplicates"],
                         [{"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2]}])

    def test_physical_rows_line_endings_bom_and_no_final_newline(self):
        base = (b"name,orders,active\r\n\r\n\"Ma\r\nya\",3,true\r\nBad,x,true\r\n"
                b"\"No\r\nra\",2,\r\nZ,3,false\r\n")
        lone_cr = base.replace(b"\r\n", b"\r")
        bom = b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + base
        no_final = base[:-2]  # drop trailing CRLF
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for data in (base, lone_cr, bom, no_final):
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 2), data)
                self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [5, 6], data)

    def test_physical_rows_multiline_reject_counts_once(self):
        # A quoted field spanning lines is one record; its error reports the
        # starting physical line. Consecutive/trailing blank lines add nothing.
        text = "name,orders,active\n\n\n\"a\nb\",nope,\n\"x\n\ny\",1,true\n\n"
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 1))
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 4)
        self.assertEqual([m.split(":", 1)[0] for m in result["errors"][0]["errors"]],
                         ["orders", "active"])
        self.assertEqual(result["records"][0]["name"], "x\n\ny")

    def test_physical_rows_whitespace_only_keeps_csv_rule(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\n   \n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["rejected"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"], ["wrong number of cells"])

    def test_source_mapping(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "display_name,purchase_count,active\nMaya,3,TRUE\n")
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.mapped_schema())
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": True}])
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 0))

    def test_source_swap_and_target_name_overlap(self):
        schema = {"columns": [
            {"name": "first", "type": "string", "source": "second"},

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, "name,orders,active\nd,4,true\n")

class CsvQuoteSyntaxTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """A quoted field left open at EOF or junk after a closing quote is a
    fatal parse error for the whole CSV, not silently folded into data."""

    UNTERMINATED = "unterminated"
    AFTER_CLOSE = "after closing quote"

    def setUp(self):
        self.schema = json.loads((ROOT / "samples/schema.json").read_text())

    def write_csv(self, directory, text):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def write_csv_bytes(self, directory, data):
        path = Path(directory) / "data.csv"
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return path

    def assert_parse_failure(self, path, start_line, reason_part):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            normalize_csv(path, self.schema)
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn("CSV parse error", message)
        self.assertIn(str(path), message)
        self.assertIn(f"record starting line {start_line}", message)
        self.assertIn(reason_part, message)
        return message

    def test_unterminated_quoted_field_at_eof(self):
        # The exact motivating input: the final quoted field never closes.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true')
            message = self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 2, self.UNTERMINATED)
            self.assertNotIn(self.AFTER_CLOSE, message)

    def test_text_after_closing_quote_is_fatal(self):
        # "Ma"ya must not collapse into the name; letters, spaces and tabs
        # right after a closing quote are all illegal.
        cases = (
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma"ya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma" ya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\n"Ma"\tya,3,true\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true"x', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true" ,\n', 2),
            ('name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\n"x"y,2,false\n', 3),
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for text, line in cases:
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
                message = self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, line, self.AFTER_CLOSE)
                self.assertNotIn(self.UNTERMINATED, message, text)

    def test_error_line_points_to_multiline_record_start(self):
        # Even though the problem is discovered on a later physical line
        # (or at EOF), the message names where the record began. Blank
        # lines and newlines inside quoted fields all occupy line numbers.
        unterminated = ("name,orders,active\n"
                        "Maya,3,true\n"
                        "\n"
                        '"a\nb",3,true\n'
                        '"x\ny,3,true')
        after_close = ("name,orders,active\n"
                       "\n\n"
                       '"a\nb",3,true\n'
                       '"x\ny"z,3,true\n')
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, unterminated)
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 6, self.UNTERMINATED)
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, after_close)
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 6, self.AFTER_CLOSE)

    def test_quote_errors_after_valid_and_ordinary_error_rows(self):
        # Earlier accepted records and ordinary row errors cannot make the
        # later quote failure a row error: the call raises, returning
        # nothing at all.
        for text in ("name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"oops,3,true\n",
                     "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"Ma\"ya,3,true\n"):
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
                self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 4, "quote")

    def test_quote_errors_in_header_report_line_one(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,"active')
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 1, self.UNTERMINATED)
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,"active"x\nMaya,3,true\n')
            self.assert_parse_failure(csv_path, 1, self.AFTER_CLOSE)

    def test_valid_commas_newlines_and_doubled_quotes(self):
        text = ('name,orders,active\n'
                '"Ma,ya",3,true\n'
                '"Ma""ya",2,true\n'
                '"No\nra",4,false\n')
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (3, 0))
        self.assertEqual([record["name"] for record in result["records"]],
                         ["Ma,ya", 'Ma"ya', "No\nra"])

    def test_valid_doubled_quote_and_eof_without_newline(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,active\n"Ma""ya",3,true')
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": 'Ma"ya', "orders": 3, "active": True}])

    def test_line_endings_bom_and_no_final_newline(self):
        variants = (
            b'name,orders,active\r\nMaya,3,"true',
            b'name,orders,active\rMaya,3,"true',
            b'\xef\xbb\xbfname,orders,active\nMaya,3,"true',
            b'name,orders,active\r\n"Ma"ya,3,true\r\n',
            b'name,orders,active\r"Ma"ya,3,true\r',
        )
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            for data in variants:
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                    normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertIn("CSV parse error", str(caught.exception), data)
            # valid quoted multiline fields under every line convention,
            # BOM and a missing final newline keep their old semantics:
            # line bytes inside a quoted field are retained verbatim.
            for data, expected_name in (
                    (b'name,orders,active\r\n"Ma\r\nya",3,true\r\n', "Ma\r\nya"),
                    (b'name,orders,active\r"Ma\rya",3,true\r', "Ma\rya"),
                    (b'\xef\xbb\xbfname,orders,active\n"Maya",3,true\n', "Maya"),
                    (b'name,orders,active\n"Maya",3,true', "Maya")):
                csv_path = self.write_csv_bytes(directory, data)
                result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
                self.assertEqual(result["accepted"], 1, data)
                self.assertEqual(result["records"][0]["name"], expected_name, data)

    def test_unquoted_double_quote_stays_literal(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, 'name,orders,active\nMa"ya,3,true\n')
            result = normalize_csv(csv_path, self.schema)
        self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": 'Ma"ya', "orders": 3, "active": True}])

    def test_cli_quote_errors_exit_two_and_keep_outputs(self):
        bad_texts = {
            "unterminated": "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"oops,3,true\n",
            "after": "name,orders,active\nMaya,3,true\nBad,x,true\n\"Ma\"ya,3,true\n",
        }
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
            for kind, text in bad_texts.items():
                csv_path = self.write_csv(directory, text)
                for fmt in (None, "csv"):
                    output.write_bytes(b"previous output bytes\n")
                    errors.write_bytes(b"previous error bytes\n")
                    run = run_cli(csv_path, output, errors, fmt=fmt)
                    self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 2, (kind, run.stderr))
                    payload = json.loads(run.stdout)
                    self.assertEqual(set(payload), {"error"})
                    self.assertTrue(payload["error"].strip())
                    self.assertIn("CSV parse error", payload["error"])
                    self.assertIn(str(csv_path), payload["error"])
                    self.assertIn("record starting line 4", payload["error"])
                    self.assertIn(kind if kind == "unterminated" else self.AFTER_CLOSE,
                                  payload["error"])
                    self.assertEqual(output.read_bytes(), b"previous output bytes\n")
                    self.assertEqual(errors.read_bytes(), b"previous error bytes\n")
            # absent outputs stay absent and no success summary is printed
            output.unlink()
            errors.unlink()
            run = run_cli(csv_path, output, errors)
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 2)
            self.assertEqual(set(json.loads(run.stdout)), {"error"})
            self.assertFalse(output.exists() or errors.exists())

    def test_cli_quote_rules_apply_to_csv_format_only(self):
        # The same characters as JSONL remain an ordinary per-line parse
        # error: exit 1, other lines processed, both outputs written.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            jsonl_path = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl"
            jsonl_path.write_text('{"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": true}\n'
                                  'Maya,3,"true\n', encoding="utf-8")
            output, errors = Path(directory) / "out.jsonl", Path(directory) / "err.jsonl"
            run = run_cli(jsonl_path, output, errors, fmt="jsonl")
            self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 1, run.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(json.loads(run.stdout), {"accepted": 1, "rejected": 1})
            self.assertEqual(len(output.read_text().splitlines()), 1)
            self.assertEqual(len(errors.read_text().splitlines()), 1)


class JsonlImporterTests(unittest.TestCase):

    def write_jsonl(self, directory, text, name="data.jsonl"):

        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def mapped_schema(self):
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True, "source": "display_name"},
            {"name": "orders", "type": "integer", "source": "purchase_count"},
            {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "required": True},
        ]}

    def test_samples_types_bom_blank_lines_and_null(self):
        result = normalize_jsonl(ROOT / "samples/customers.jsonl", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 0))
        self.assertEqual(result["records"][0], {"name": "Maya", "orders": 3, "active": True})
        self.assertIsNone(result["records"][1]["orders"])

    def test_mixed_sample_row_numbers_and_counts(self):
        result = normalize_jsonl(ROOT / "samples/mixed.jsonl", self.schema)
        self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 2))
        self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [3, 4])
        self.assertTrue(any("orders" in message for message in result["errors"][0]["errors"]))
        self.assertTrue(any("name" in message for message in result["errors"][1]["errors"]))

    def test_empty_and_blank_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            empty = self.write_jsonl(directory, "", "empty.jsonl")
            blanks = self.write_jsonl(directory, "\n   \n\t\n", "blanks.jsonl")
            for path in (empty, blanks):
                result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
                self.assertEqual(result, {"records": [], "errors": [], "accepted": 0, "rejected": 0})

    def test_physical_row_numbers_skip_blank_lines(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            path = self.write_jsonl(directory, '{"name": "A", "orders": 1, "active": true}\n\nnot json\n  \n[]\n')
            result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
            self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]], [3, 5])
            self.assertTrue(result["errors"][0]["errors"][0].startswith("parse error"))
            self.assertTrue(result["errors"][1]["errors"][0].startswith("structure error"))

    def test_string_trimming_empty_and_required_rules(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            path = self.write_jsonl(directory,
                                   '{"name": "  ", "orders": null, "active": true}\n'
                                   '{"name": "ok", "orders": "", "active": "FALSE"}\n'
                                   '{"name": "Z", "orders": "  ", "active": " True "}\n')
            result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, 1))
            self.assertEqual(result["records"][0], {"name": "ok", "orders": None, "active": False})
            self.assertEqual(result["records"][1], {"name": "Z", "orders": None, "active": True})
            self.assertTrue(any("name" in message for message in result["errors"][0]["errors"]))

    def test_integer_rules(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            accepted = '{"name": "ok", "orders": %s, "active": true}'
            rejected_values = ("3.0", "1e2", "-0.5", "true", '"3.5"', '"1e2"', "[3]")
            lines = [accepted % "42", accepted % '"-8"']
            lines.extend(accepted % value for value in rejected_values)
            path = self.write_jsonl(directory, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
            result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (2, len(rejected_values)))
            self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in result["records"]], [42, -8])
            for row in result["errors"]:
                self.assertTrue(any("orders" in message for message in row["errors"]))

    def test_boolean_rules(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            lines = ['{"name": "a", "orders": null, "active": true}',
                     '{"name": "b", "orders": null, "active": false}',
                     '{"name": "c", "orders": null, "active": "TrUe"}',
                     '{"name": "d", "orders": null, "active": 1}',
                     '{"name": "e", "orders": null, "active": "yes"}',
                     '{"name": "f", "orders": null, "active": ["true"]}']
            path = self.write_jsonl(directory, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
            result = normalize_jsonl(path, self.schema)
            self.assertEqual([record["active"] for record in result["records"]], [True, False, True])
            self.assertEqual(result["rejected"], 3)

1	# Data Importer
2	
3	Normalize a CSV file or JSONL stream to JSONL using a small explicit schema. Requires Python 3.10+; no installation dependencies.
4	
5	`python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.csv --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl` converts the two valid CSV rows. The input format is chosen explicitly with `--format csv` (default) or `--format jsonl`; it is never inferred from the file extension. For JSONL, use `python3 data_importer.py samples/customers.jsonl --schema samples/schema.json --output customers.jsonl --errors errors.jsonl --format jsonl`. `samples/mixed.csv` and `samples/mixed.jsonl` each contain one accepted row and two rejected rows. Each rejected row is written separately with its physical line number (for CSV the header is line 1) and its errors; accepted rows remain available in input order.
6	
7	Schema columns specify name, type (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`), optional `required`, and an optional target-typed `default` (see below). A column may also declare an optional `source`: the CSV column, or JSONL object key, it reads from, while `name` remains the output field name; omitting `source` reads the field named by `name`. An explicit `source` must be a non-empty, non-blank string, and the effective source names must be unique across columns (a source may coincide with another field's `name`, and two fields may swap sources). For CSV the header must match the effective source names and their order exactly, compared literally without trimming or case folding. For JSONL each non-empty line must hold exactly one JSON object whose key set equals the effective source set exactly (order is free, keys match literally); missing or extra keys reject the line.
8	
9	CSV text is trimmed, absent optional values become JSON null, and booleans accept true/false without case sensitivity. CSV quote syntax is checked strictly for both the header and every data record: two double quotes inside a quoted field still denote one literal double quote, and a double quote inside an unquoted field stays an ordinary character, but a quoted field that is still open when the file ends, or any character other than a comma, a line ending or the end of the file appearing immediately after a closing quote (a space or tab included), aborts the whole parse rather than being folded into the cell value. `normalize_csv` raises `ValueError` whose message contains "CSV parse error", the input path, the offending record's starting physical line and a reason distinguishing the two problems (the header starts at line 1; a data record starts on the physical line after the preceding read record ends, so blank lines and newlines inside quoted fields shift it, and an error detected only on a later line or at EOF still points at the record start); no partial result is returned. On the CLI (the default format or explicit `--format csv`) such an error exits 2 with standard output carrying only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string carries that message (no success summary), and both outputs keep their pre-run state — existing files keep their bytes, previously absent files are not created, and the input and schema are untouched — regardless of valid records or ordinary row errors read earlier. (Ordinary per-row errors — type, required, enum or cell-count problems — still leave other rows valid and exit 1; quote-syntax failures are the only CSV parse errors that abort the run.) JSONL is read as UTF-8, allowing a leading byte-order mark; blank lines are skipped while still consuming a physical line number, and an empty or all-blank file reports zero counts. Each line is parsed independently: invalid JSON, a non-object top-level value, duplicate top-level keys, and the `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity` constants reject that line and later lines are still processed. String values are trimmed; trimmed-to-empty strings and JSON null follow the same required/null rule as CSV. The `string` type accepts JSON strings only; `integer` accepts non-boolean JSON integers or strings convertible under the CSV rule (fractional and exponential JSON numbers are rejected); `boolean` accepts JSON booleans or case-insensitive `true`/`false` strings. Arrays, objects and any other value never convert implicitly and are reported as field errors. Error messages distinguish parse, structure and field errors; field errors use the output field name and are collected in schema order. Output objects use sorted keys. The input is processed in memory. Outputs replace existing files but cannot alias either input or each other; this is checked before either input is read or either output is written. Identity ignores file names, extensions and directories: two paths alias when they resolve to the same pathname (identical paths, relative or absolute, including symbolic links) or, when both currently exist, when they are the same file on disk (the same device and inode, so two distinct names hard-linked to one file alias it); two independent files with identical contents are not aliases. An output that does not exist yet only takes part in the resolved-pathname comparison. An alias conflict exits 2 with standard output carrying only a JSON object whose non-empty `error` string names the paths that point to the same file (no accepted/rejected summary); the source, schema and both outputs stay exactly as they were — existing files keep their bytes, hard-link relationships and symbolic links themselves are untouched, and absent outputs are not created. Parent output directories must already exist and are never created. CLI exit codes are 0 for no rejected rows, 1 for row errors and 2 for an invalid format or configuration (including mapping, header or key-set mismatches), unreadable input, an alias conflict, or other I/O errors (including a path that cannot be resolved or stated); in that case standard output carries only a JSON object with a non-empty `error` string naming the failing target path (no success summary) and existing output files are left untouched (and absent ones are not created).
10	
11	A column may declare an optional `default` written as a value of the target type: `string` defaults must be strings whose trimmed value is non-empty (the trimmed value is what gets emitted), `integer` defaults must be non-boolean integers, and `boolean` defaults must be booleans (`0` and `false` are valid). `null`, arrays, objects and anything else not matching the declared type — including a blank string — is a configuration error: the API raises `ValueError` (naming both `default` and the output field) before the input is read, even when no row would have needed it, and the CLI exits 2 with only a JSON `error` object on standard output, leaving both output files exactly as they were (absent ones stay absent); the caller's schema object is never mutated. def _prepare_ranges(columns, defaults):
    """Validate the optional ``minimum``/``maximum`` bounds of integer columns.

    Returns a mapping of output field name to a (minimum, maximum) pair
    where either end is None when undeclared. Bounds may appear on
    ``integer`` columns only and each must be a non-boolean integer
    (negative and zero are legal); a declared minimum above the declared
    maximum, and a processed default outside the range, are configuration
    errors even when no row would use the default. Raises ValueError
    naming the output field, the attribute and the offending value before
    the input is read; the caller's schema is never mutated.
    """
    ranges = {}
    for column in columns:
        name, kind = column["name"], column["type"]
        bounds = {}
        for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
            if attribute not in column:
                continue
            value = column[attribute]
            if kind != "integer":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {value!r} requires an integer column")
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column {name!r} {attribute} {value!r} must be a non-boolean integer")
            bounds[attribute] = value
        if not bounds:
            continue
        minimum = bounds.get("minimum")
        maximum = bounds.get("maximum")
        if minimum is not None and maximum is not None and minimum > maximum:
            raise ValueError(
                f"column {name!r} minimum {minimum!r} is greater than maximum {maximum!r}")
        if name in defaults:
            default = defaults[name]
            if minimum is not None and default < minimum:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is less than minimum {minimum!r}")
            if maximum is not None and default > maximum:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column {name!r} default {default!r} is greater than maximum {maximum!r}")
        ranges[name] = (minimum, maximum)
    return ranges

class MissingValuesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """A column may declare text markers that count as missing values."""

    def marker_schema(self, **orders_overrides):
        column = {"name": "orders", "type": "integer", "missing_values": ["N/A"]}
        column.update(orders_overrides)
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True},
            column,
            {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "required": True},
        ]}

    def write_source(self, directory, text, fmt):
        path = Path(directory) / ("data.csv" if fmt == "csv" else "data.jsonl")
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def normalize(self, path, schema, fmt, **kwargs):
        return (normalize_csv if fmt == "csv" else normalize_jsonl)(path, schema, **kwargs)

    ENUM_ROWS = {
        "csv": ("name,orders,active\n"
                "a, N/A ,true\n"
                "b,3,true\n"
                "c,0,false\n"
                "d,4,true\n"
                "e,bad,true\n"),
        "jsonl": ('{"name": "a", "orders": " N/A ", "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "b", "orders": "3", "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "c", "orders": 0, "active": false}\n'
                  '{"name": "d", "orders": 4, "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "e", "orders": "bad", "active": true}\n'),
    }

    def test_marker_default_enum_and_type_error(self):
        # " N/A " and "3" both become 3 via the default, 0 stays 0,
        # 4 hits the enum and "bad" hits the integer type error.
        schema = self.marker_schema(default=3, allowed_values=[0, 3])
        for fmt in ("csv", "jsonl"):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, self.ENUM_ROWS[fmt], fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (3, 2))
            self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in result["records"]], [3, 3, 0])
            self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]],
                             [5, 6] if fmt == "csv" else [4, 5])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["orders: value 4 is not one of allowed_values [0, 3]"])
            type_error = result["errors"][1]["errors"]
            self.assertEqual(len(type_error), 1)
            self.assertTrue(type_error[0].startswith("orders:"))
            self.assertNotIn("allowed_values", type_error[0])

    def test_marker_match_is_case_sensitive(self):
        # Declaring "n/a" does not match the input "N/A".
        schema = self.marker_schema(missing_values=["n/a"], default=3)
        for fmt, text in (
                ("csv", "name,orders,active\na,N/A,true\nb,n/a,true\n"),
                ("jsonl", '{"name": "a", "orders": "N/A", "active": true}\n'
                         '{"name": "b", "orders": "n/a", "active": true}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 1))
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": "b", "orders": 3, "active": True}])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["row"], 2 if fmt == "csv" else 1)
            self.assertTrue(result["errors"][0]["errors"][0].startswith("orders:"))

    def test_marker_without_default_null_or_required(self):
        optional = self.marker_schema()
        required = self.marker_schema(required=True)
        for fmt, text in (
                ("csv", "name,orders,active\na,N/A,true\nb,2,true\n"),
                ("jsonl", '{"name": "a", "orders": "N/A", "active": true}\n'
                         '{"name": "b", "orders": 2, "active": true}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                null_result = self.normalize(path, optional, fmt)
                required_result = self.normalize(path, required, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((null_result["accepted"], null_result["rejected"]), (2, 0))

class IntegerRangeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """An integer column may declare inclusive minimum/maximum bounds."""

    def range_schema(self, **orders_overrides):
        column = {"name": "orders", "type": "integer",
                  "minimum": 0, "maximum": 5, "default": 3,
                  "missing_values": ["N/A"]}
        column.update(orders_overrides)
        return {"columns": [
            {"name": "name", "type": "string", "required": True},
            column,
            {"name": "active", "type": "boolean", "required": True},
        ]}

    def write_source(self, directory, text, fmt):
        path = Path(directory) / ("data.csv" if fmt == "csv" else "data.jsonl")
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def normalize(self, path, schema, fmt, **kwargs):
        return (normalize_csv if fmt == "csv" else normalize_jsonl)(path, schema, **kwargs)

    RANGE_ROWS = {
        "csv": ("name,orders,active\n"
                "a,0,true\n"
                "b,3,true\n"
                "c,5,false\n"
                "d,-1,true\n"
                "e,6,true\n"
                "f,bad,true\n"
                "g, N/A ,true\n"),
        "jsonl": ('{"name": "a", "orders": "0", "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "b", "orders": 3, "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "c", "orders": 5, "active": false}\n'
                  '{"name": "d", "orders": -1, "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "e", "orders": 6, "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "f", "orders": "bad", "active": true}\n'
                  '{"name": "g", "orders": " N/A ", "active": true}\n'),
    }

    def test_range_default_marker_and_type_error(self):
        # "0"/"3"/"5" convert, " N/A " hits the marker and takes the
        # default 3, -1 and 6 are out of range, "bad" is a type error.
        schema = self.range_schema()
        for fmt in ("csv", "jsonl"):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, self.RANGE_ROWS[fmt], fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (4, 3))
            self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in result["records"]],
                             [0, 3, 5, 3])
            self.assertEqual([row["row"] for row in result["errors"]],
                             [5, 6, 7] if fmt == "csv" else [4, 5, 6])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["orders: value -1 is less than minimum 0"])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][1]["errors"],
                             ["orders: value 6 is greater than maximum 5"])
            type_error = result["errors"][2]["errors"]
            self.assertEqual(len(type_error), 1)
            self.assertTrue(type_error[0].startswith("orders:"))
            self.assertNotIn("minimum", type_error[0])
            self.assertNotIn("maximum", type_error[0])

    def test_range_precedes_filter_and_duplicates_count_kept_records(self):
        schema = self.range_schema()
        for fmt in ("csv", "jsonl"):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, self.RANGE_ROWS[fmt], fmt)
                filtered = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt,
                                          filter_eq={"field": "orders", "value": 3})
                duplicates = self.normalize(
                    path, schema, fmt, duplicate_by=["orders"],
                    filter_eq={"field": "orders", "value": 3})
            # out-of-range rows are rejected, never filtered
            self.assertEqual((filtered["accepted"], filtered["filtered"],
                              filtered["rejected"]), (2, 2, 3))
            self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in filtered["records"]], [3, 3])
            self.assertEqual(duplicates["duplicates"],
                             [{"key": {"orders": 3}, "record_numbers": [1, 2]}])

    def test_equal_bounds_accept_only_that_integer(self):
        schema = self.range_schema(minimum=3, maximum=3)
        for fmt, text in (
                ("csv", "name,orders,active\na,3,true\nb,2,true\nc,4,true\n"),
                ("jsonl", '{"name": "a", "orders": 3, "active": true}\n'
                         '{"name": "b", "orders": 2, "active": true}\n'
                         '{"name": "c", "orders": 4, "active": true}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 2))
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"name": "a", "orders": 3, "active": True}])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["orders: value 2 is less than minimum 3"])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][1]["errors"],
                             ["orders: value 4 is greater than maximum 3"])

    def test_one_sided_and_negative_bounds(self):
        floor_only = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer", "minimum": -2}]}
        ceiling_only = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer", "maximum": 0}]}
        for fmt, text in (
                ("csv", "n\n-2\n-3\n5\n"),
                ("jsonl", '{"n": -2}\n{"n": -3}\n{"n": 5}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                floor = self.normalize(path, floor_only, fmt)
                ceiling = self.normalize(path, ceiling_only, fmt)
            self.assertEqual([record["n"] for record in floor["records"]], [-2, 5])
            self.assertEqual(floor["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["n: value -3 is less than minimum -2"])
            self.assertEqual([record["n"] for record in ceiling["records"]], [-2, -3])
            self.assertEqual(ceiling["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["n: value 5 is greater than maximum 0"])

    def test_null_and_empty_follow_the_ordinary_rules(self):
        optional = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer", "minimum": 1}]}
        required = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer", "minimum": 1,
                                 "required": True}]}
        for fmt, text in (("csv", "n\n\n"), ("jsonl", '{"n": null}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                null_result = self.normalize(path, optional, fmt)
                required_result = self.normalize(path, required, fmt)
            self.assertEqual(null_result["records"], [{"n": None}])
            self.assertEqual(null_result["rejected"], 0)
            self.assertEqual(required_result["rejected"], 1)
            self.assertEqual(required_result["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["n: required value is empty"])

    def test_enum_may_list_out_of_range_integers(self):
        # An allowed_values entry outside the range is not a configuration
        # error; records must still satisfy both checks.
        schema = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer",
                               "minimum": 0, "maximum": 5,
                               "allowed_values": [3, 9]}]}
        for fmt, text in (
                ("csv", "n\n3\n9\n4\n"),
                ("jsonl", '{"n": 3}\n{"n": 9}\n{"n": 4}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual((result["accepted"], result["rejected"]), (1, 2))
            self.assertEqual(result["records"], [{"n": 3}])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"],
                             ["n: value 9 is greater than maximum 5"])
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][1]["errors"],
                             ["n: value 4 is not one of allowed_values [3, 9]"])

    def test_multi_field_errors_keep_schema_order(self):
        schema = {"columns": [
            {"name": "a", "type": "integer", "minimum": 0},
            {"name": "b", "type": "integer", "maximum": 10},
        ]}
        for fmt, text in (("csv", "a,b\n-1,11\n"),
                          ("jsonl", '{"a": -1, "b": 11}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual(result["errors"][0]["errors"], [
                "a: value -1 is less than minimum 0",
                "b: value 11 is greater than maximum 10",
            ])

    def test_invalid_bounds_raise_before_reading(self):
        import copy
        missing = ROOT / "samples" / "does-not-exist.csv"
        # bounds on non-integer columns are configuration errors
        for kind in ("string", "boolean"):
            for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
                schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": kind, attribute: 1}]}
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                    normalize_csv(missing, schema)
                message = str(caught.exception)
                self.assertIn("f", message)
                self.assertIn(attribute, message)
                self.assertIn("1", message)
        # bounds must be non-boolean integers; negative and zero are legal
        for attribute in ("minimum", "maximum"):
            for bad in (None, "3", 3.0, True, [3], {"x": 1}):
                schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": "integer",
                                       attribute: bad}]}
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                    normalize_jsonl(ROOT / "samples" / "does-not-exist.jsonl", schema)
                message = str(caught.exception)
                self.assertIn("f", message, (attribute, bad))
                self.assertIn(attribute, message, (attribute, bad))
                self.assertIn(repr(bad), message, (attribute, bad))
        for attribute, value in (("minimum", -4), ("maximum", 0)):
            schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": "integer", attribute: value}]}
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, "f\n-4\n", "csv")
                self.assertEqual(normalize_csv(path, schema)["rejected"], 0)
        # minimum above maximum is a configuration error
        schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": "integer",
                               "minimum": 5, "maximum": 5}]}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            path = self.write_source(directory, "f\n5\n", "csv")
            self.assertEqual(normalize_csv(path, schema)["records"], [{"f": 5}])
        schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": "integer",
                               "minimum": 6, "maximum": 5}]}
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
            normalize_csv(missing, schema)
        message = str(caught.exception)
        self.assertIn("f", message)
        self.assertIn("minimum", message)
        self.assertIn("maximum", message)
        # a default outside the range is a configuration error even when
        # no record would use it
        for default, bounds in ((4, {"minimum": 5}), (6, {"maximum": 5}),
                                (0, {"minimum": 1, "maximum": 5})):
            schema = {"columns": [{"name": "f", "type": "integer",
                                   "default": default, **bounds}]}
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as caught:
                normalize_csv(missing, schema)
            message = str(caught.exception)
            self.assertIn("f", message, (default, bounds))
            self.assertIn("default", message, (default, bounds))
            self.assertIn(repr(default), message, (default, bounds))
        # the caller's schema is never mutated
        schema = self.range_schema()
        snapshot = copy.deepcopy(schema)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
            path = self.write_source(directory, self.RANGE_ROWS["csv"], "csv")
            normalize_csv(path, schema)
        self.assertEqual(schema, snapshot)

    def test_columns_without_bounds_are_unchanged(self):
        schema = {"columns": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}]}
        for fmt, text in (("csv", "n\n-99\n1000000\n"),
                          ("jsonl", '{"n": -99}\n{"n": 1000000}\n')):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                path = self.write_source(directory, text, fmt)
                result = self.normalize(path, schema, fmt)
            self.assertEqual(result, {"records": [{"n": -99}, {"n": 1000000}],
                                      "errors": [], "accepted": 2, "rejected": 0})

    def run_cli(self, source, schema_path, output, errors, fmt):
        command = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "data_importer.py"), str(source),
                   "--schema", str(schema_path),
                   "--output", str(output), "--errors", str(errors),
                   "--format", fmt]
        return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)

    def test_cli_row_errors_exit_one_and_export(self):
        for fmt in ("csv", "jsonl"):
            with self.subTest(fmt=fmt), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                source = self.write_source(directory, self.RANGE_ROWS[fmt], fmt)
                schema_path = Path(directory) / "schema.json"
                schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(self.range_schema()), encoding="utf-8")
                output, errors = Path(directory) / "data.jsonl", Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl"
                run = self.run_cli(source, schema_path, output, errors, fmt)
                self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 1, run.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(json.loads(run.stdout), {"accepted": 4, "rejected": 3})
                records = [json.loads(line) for line in output.read_text().splitlines()]
                self.assertEqual([record["orders"] for record in records], [0, 3, 5, 3])
                self.assertEqual(len(errors.read_text().splitlines()), 3)

    def test_cli_bad_range_exit_two_keeps_files(self):
        bad_schemas = (
            {"columns": [{"name": "orders", "type": "integer",
                          "minimum": 6, "maximum": 5}]},
            {"columns": [{"name": "orders", "type": "integer", "minimum": "0"}]},
            {"columns": [{"name": "name", "type": "string", "maximum": 3}]},
            {"columns": [{"name": "orders", "type": "integer",
                          "minimum": 0, "default": -1}]},
        )
        for fmt in ("csv", "jsonl"):
            for bad_schema in bad_schemas:
                with self.subTest(fmt=fmt, schema=bad_schema), \
                        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT) as directory:
                    source = self.write_source(directory, self.RANGE_ROWS[fmt], fmt)
                    schema_path = Path(directory) / "schema.json"
                    schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(bad_schema), encoding="utf-8")
                    output, errors = (Path(directory) / "data.jsonl",
                                      Path(directory) / "errors.jsonl")
                    output.write_text("keep me\n", encoding="utf-8")
                    run = self.run_cli(source, schema_path, output, errors, fmt)
                    self.assertEqual(run.returncode, 2, run.stderr)
                    payload = json.loads(run.stdout)
                    self.assertEqual(set(payload), {"error"})
                    self.assertTrue(payload["error"].strip())
                    self.assertEqual(output.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), "keep me\n")
                    self.assertFalse(errors.exists())
